observations: Six accepted Indigenous-led candidates meet the representation gate without treating any single tribal institution as a universal Wampanoag voice.
Primary accounts deliberately include conflicting colonial framings and an Indigenous primary text; disagreement is modeled, not reconciled.
Every accepted candidate has a bounded locator strategy and begins as metadata-and-link-only except the Library of Congress map's stated free-use item.
All six contextual collection families can be preserved or expanded without publishing any historical object during this gate.

retainedLimitations: The Mourt's Relation account remains outside this regional acquisition purpose.
Transatlantic orphan places remain outside the geographic boundary.

reviewFindings.issue: Narragansett Bay and Great Swamp are connected conflict edges, not permission for a Narragansett regional corpus.
reviewFindings.requiredAction: Limit objects to direct Wampanoag-network connections and retain Narragansett identities and accounts distinctly.

reviewFindings.issue: Mashpee archival materials require collection-level permission and culturally appropriate access.
reviewFindings.requiredAction: Contact the archive; register no item until an archive-supplied identifier, access decision, and rights basis exist.

reviewFindings.issue: Easton, Mather, Hubbard, and later editions are distinct works, witnesses, and editorial layers.
reviewFindings.requiredAction: Preserve original-work, edition, transcription, and digital-surrogate identities separately.

reviewFindings.issue: Site evidence cannot by itself establish a named seventeenth-century political identity or territorial boundary.
reviewFindings.requiredAction: Use archaeology as qualified contextual evidence and prohibit identity inference.

reviewFindings.issue: The 1681 Mittark petition and later memory scholarship fall outside the 1614–1676 core.
reviewFindings.requiredAction: Use only in marked continuity, memory, or aftermath structures.

reviewFindings.issue: The existing corpus concentrates reporting in the NMAI timeline and 33 claims have one reporting lineage.
reviewFindings.requiredAction: Cap projected use per new source, require independent lineages, and do not count a second edition as independence.

scope.backgroundRule: Earlier archaeological evidence and post-1676 continuity may appear only as explicitly attributed context, not as core event claims.
scope.geographicBoundary: Cape Cod and Noepe through Manomet and Nemasket to Pokanoket, Mount Hope, Pocasset, and Sakonnet; the Narragansett Bay edge appears only where directly connected.
scope.title: Wampanoag Homelands and Intercommunity Networks, 1614–1676

sourceConcentration.rule: No source may report more than four of the 28 projected claims without a documented exception and an independent lineage.

unresolvedChronologyQuestions: Which Epenow kidnapping/return dates reflect distinct events or differing accounts?
Which dates for Wamsutta's final journey and death can be represented only as uncertain or contested?
Which war-event dates differ because sources use report date, event date, or later retrospective chronology?
unresolvedGeographicQuestions: Which archive-supported place relations connect Manomet and Nemasket without implying fixed territorial polygons?
Where should the Narragansett Bay edge stop when an account leaves the Wampanoag network?
Which Noepe and Cape Cod place names require community-preferred canonical forms and colonial aliases?
unresolvedIdentityQuestions: Which historical labels in colonial records refer to communities, places, offices, or imposed aggregates?
How should Epenow-related Chappaquiddick and Aquinnah accounts coexist without unsupported identity reconciliation?
Which person and office references in deeds or petitions require tribal review before canonical IDs are proposed?
